name: Ashoka Halwa (Mung Bean Pudding)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 1 pinch red food colouring in 1 tsp water

steps: Dry roast the moong dal until it smells nutty and browns slightly.
Add 3 cups of water and pressure cook for about 7–8 whistles until the dal is soft and mushy.
Add 4 tbsp ghee to a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat, and cook the wheat flour in it until golden brown.
Stir the cooked dal into the flour mixture, and let it thicken for 5 minutes. Add the sugar.

Stirring continuously, start mixing in the remaining ghee 1 tbsp at a time. Keep stirring until the mixture starts leaving the sides of the pan and the whole mixture forms a dough. It will take about 12–15 minutes and 6–7 tbsp of ghee.
Heat 1 tbsp of ghee in a separate frying pan, and add the cashews. Fry until slightly brown, then add to the halwa mixture.
Mix in the powdered cardamom and food color.
Remove from the heat and let cool.

culture.text: Ashoka Halwa or Pasi Paruppu Halwa is a thick gooey sweet from Thiruvaiyaru, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India. Ashoka Halwa consists of Moong Dal, ghee, sugar and water, flavored with cardamom and cashews or almonds. It is known for it thick texture and rich red, yellow and orange colour.
